title: What do technical writers do: solving workflow clarification for Mac teams

description: Technical writers spend most of their time clarifying workflows. Learn why this happens, what it costs your team, and how to fix it on your Mac.
intro: Technical writers spend their time researching products, interviewing experts, and documenting complex systems. Many people ask what do technical writers do all day, and the answer is often that they spend most of their time clarifying workflows rather than writing. This ambiguity creates bottlenecks that slow down product releases and frustrate engineering teams.
tldr: Technical writers spend only 10% to 30% of their time on actual writing.
Workflow clarification is the process of defining steps and ownership for documentation.
Ambiguity leads to excessive detective work, chasing SMEs, and project delays.
Fixes include formalizing handover standards and using centralized tracking tools.

blocks.text: Why technical writer workflow clarification is a constant battle

When you ask what do technical writers do, the answer often involves a lot of detective work. Workflow clarification is the process of mapping out who does what, when, and how. Without a clear plan, you spend your day chasing down Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) to ask simple questions. This happens because documentation is often an afterthought in the development cycle. You are left to reconstruct features from incomplete notes or oral history.
The hidden costs of unclear documentation processes

Ambiguity has a high price tag. When you do not have a clear workflow, you end up doing redundant work. You might write a guide for a feature that changes the next day because you were not part of the initial planning. This rework wastes your time and forces you to miss deadlines. If your team relies on email for approvals, documents get lost in chains. This forces you to spend hours searching for the latest version instead of writing.
How to fix workflow bottlenecks on your Mac

You can fix these issues without spending money on new software. Start by defining a formal handover process. Tell your team that you need a briefing pack before you start a task. This pack should include the user goals, known constraints, and relevant permissions. Use a shared space like Notion or Google Docs to keep these requirements in one place. This prevents the back and forth that usually happens over Slack or email.

faq.question: What do technical writers do if they are not writing?
faq.answer: They spend most of their time researching products, interviewing subject matter experts, attending meetings, and managing documentation projects.

faq.question: How can I improve my technical writing workflow on a Mac?
faq.answer: Adopt a structured content approach, use tools like Obsidian or Notion for organization, and establish clear handover requirements with your engineering team.
